anti_overlap: Focuses on GPU pipeline, WASM constraints, and framework selection — not tile engine spatial logic (fd-isometric-tile-engine-architecture), ASCII art vocabulary and aesthetics (fd-ascii-art-game-aesthetics), glyph rasterization mathematics (fd-glyph-geometry-rasterization), or WASM binary size/startup (fd-wasm-target-feasibility)
decision_lens: Can the chosen rendering stack (wgpu vs bevy vs macroquad vs pixels) deliver 60fps for a 2D isometric scene with 200+ animated ASCII-textured entities in a WASM browser context? What are the actual memory and draw-call budgets? Where does the framework abstraction help and where does it impose unacceptable overhead?
focus: wgpu and Rust graphics ecosystem for WASM/browser rendering: WebGPU/WebGL2 fallback, shader compilation, texture management, frame budgets, and the specific constraints of running a custom 2D renderer in the browser through wasm-bindgen
name: fd-wgpu-wasm-render-pipeline
persona: Rust graphics systems programmer who has shipped wgpu applications targeting both native and WASM; knows the WebGPU spec gaps, wasm-bindgen memory constraints, shader cross-compilation via naga, and the real-world performance characteristics of wgpu-in-browser versus native. Has benchmarked macroquad, bevy, and raw wgpu for 2D tile rendering workloads.
review_areas: Framework selection tradeoffs: raw wgpu gives maximum control but requires building a 2D renderer from scratch; bevy provides a full ECS+renderer but may conflict with hecs; macroquad is simple but WASM support has known texture memory leaks; pixels is CPU-only which simplifies but limits — does the chosen stack match the project's actual constraints?

WebGPU vs WebGL2 fallback: wgpu targets WebGPU in browsers but Safari/Firefox support is incomplete as of 2025; the WebGL2 backend has different shader constraints and performance characteristics — is there a tested fallback path?

WASM memory constraints: WASM linear memory defaults to 256MB with 4GB max; texture atlases for pre-rasterized ASCII glyphs plus tile maps plus entity sprites must fit within this — is the memory budget calculated and enforced?

Shader cross-compilation: wgsl shaders compiled via naga for WebGPU work differently than the WebGL2 GLSL output; custom 2D shaders for character rendering (SDF text, color manipulation, depth effects) must be tested on both backends

Frame budget accounting: at 60fps in WASM, the frame budget is 16.6ms but JavaScript GC pauses and wasm-bindgen overhead steal 2-4ms; the actual rendering budget is closer to 12ms — does the architecture account for this with a frame budget profiler?

severity_examples.condition: wgpu WASM build targets WebGPU only with no adapter fallback to webgl2 feature flag
severity_examples.scenario: The game renders a black screen on Safari because WebGPU is not available and no WebGL2 fallback is configured, excluding a significant portion of the browser audience

severity_examples.condition: No texture cache eviction policy; glyph atlas grows monotonically
severity_examples.scenario: WASM memory grows unbounded as new ASCII glyph textures are rasterized on demand and never evicted, causing an OOM crash after 30 minutes of gameplay

severity_examples.condition: Shaders not tested on WebGL2 backend; no precision qualifiers specified
severity_examples.scenario: Custom depth-coloring fragment shader works perfectly in native wgpu but produces different color output on WebGL2 backend due to precision differences in mediump float

success_hints: The acid test: open the game in Chrome (WebGPU), Firefox (WebGL2 fallback), and Safari (WebGL2 fallback). All three should render the same scene at >30fps. Open the browser memory profiler and play for 10 minutes — memory should plateau, not climb. If all three pass, the rendering pipeline is production-viable.
task_context: Elf Revel — Rust/WASM colony sim evaluating wgpu-based spatial ASCII rendering. Current codebase uses hecs ECS and rust_pixel for TUI. Proposed paradigm shift requires a browser-capable GPU rendering pipeline that can composite ASCII glyphs as spatial textures. Must work across browsers.
